So, I've played this game for a few hours. Is it fun? Sure! Is it a bit stale? Sure! This game can be a time sink to distract you from other things in your life. Best played with friends in an invite only session. If you grind hard enough, purchase the businesses, and dedicate some time to running said businesses and selling goods, you can become a rich player in the game with access to all of the expensive stuff in the game.

Early on, it is a bit of a slog to get things in order. A bit overwhelming at first, but again, if you spend some time running heists, hanging with friends, and staying diligent with your businesses (notably the Nightclub, bunker, and warehouses) you will have a good time.

Avoid public lobbies which are completely overrun with modders that can and will ruin your gaming experience. They can dump a bunch of hacked cash on you, level you up way too high, perform annoying actions on your character, and brick/corrupt your character. None of these things are fun nor are they enhancing your experience in any way. Avoid them all. The cash may be tempting, but you can earn quite a substantial sum of cash from just playing and grinding.

Definitely one of my most favorite games of all time. The story mode was amazing. The protagonists were very likeable. The only problem however was that the story mode was too short but there are many things you can do in between and work on in-game achievements etc.

Then there is the GTAOnline side of it where the player can create two characters and have a huge variety of missions to do, awesome stuff to buy. Housing, cars, businesses, motorcycle clubs, nightclubs etc. Definitely a joy to play alone and with your friends.

My favorite feature however, is the Rockstar Editor where you can create videos, movies of characters and use the built-in game editor to work your magic of bringing the characters alive. This game is a MUST have. Its definitely way up there on the top of my list of favorites.

GTA V is honestly one of the best games I’ve played. The story is solid and fun, but what I really love is just messing around in the open world. Driving, flying, doing random stuff, or jumping into chaos—it's never boring.

The missions are cool, and I liked switching between the three characters. Trevor is insane (in a good way), Michael's got drama, and Franklin’s just chill. I didn’t even rush the story—I took my time, explored a lot, and it was still super fun.

But where the game really shines for me is GTA Online. That’s where I’ve spent most of my time. I love grinding heists, CEO work, Cayo Perico, or just doing random missions with people I meet in public lobbies. It’s fun, chaotic, and feels like there’s always something to do. Yeah, sometimes it's grindy, but making money, buying cool stuff, and leveling up actually feels worth it.

If you like free roam games where you can do whatever you want, make money, and cause some chaos—this is 100% worth playing. Even in 2025, it still holds up really well.

Fun Fact: Whenever your connected to the internet and playing this game, you ip address is being globally broadcast through the rockstar launcher. This means other players with mod menus can set alerts to notify them whenever you go online. They can then force their way into your lobby, even if private, and troll you until they get bored. Rockstar is aware of this issue, but for some reason wont address it.
DO NOT PLAY ONLINE WITHOUT A VPN.

Even if you can get past all that, the state of pc online is so distraught that it makes the game unplayable. There are modders in every public lobby, so your either constantly getting spawn killed and cant get anything done, or the lobby will be so glitchy that it will eventually crash and kick you, or force close the game.

The only way this game is tolerable is in a private lobby. Doing this will cut out most in game content though, as most content is only available for play if your in a public lobby. Playing in a private lobby, in my opinion, also defeats the purpose of playing an online game; unless you are only playing with a set group and you are all only on at the same time.

Even 8 years later, this game is easily one of the best that you can buy.

Whilst GTA Online has gone in a direction I don't like — and wouldn't really recommend in engaging very much with to complete newcomers by this stage — I can't ignore that it still has thousands of hours to offer players across a variety of different activities — there's something for everyone in GTA Online and it will also make them money whilst they're at it.

Single Player is also undeniably a brilliant experience. Even though it will take you a while to get through to the end of the story, there's really no excuse for not playing it through at least once.

A lot of us have got a bit tired of this game in the many years since it's original release, but from an objective point of view, even if this game released for the very first time this year, it would still be one of the best video games ever made and blow us all away.

The driving is much easier than GTA 4, literally anyone can be a decent driver in GTA 5 unless you have brain damage, but I guess it makes it more accessible, lol. Shooting is also much improved and is high quality, and those two elements combined with many others, including but not limited to the excellent map, make this game a perfect sandbox.

At this point, we should have the choice to download the single player mode or GTA Online separately. Unless you have plenty of extra storage space, it's difficult to justify revisiting the story if you must sacrifice 50-60GB to a mode that has been milked bone dry, oversaturated with microtransactions and chock-full of hackers. For anyone who hasn't experienced GTA V, they're probably better off buying a secondhand copy for PS4 or XBONE and playing it completely offline, because an 11 year old single player game has no reason being over 100GB.
There is no doubt that GTA VI will be a massive game, so hopefully Rockstar will finally provide the single player and online modes as separate clients. Considering Rockstar and 2K's decisions over the past decade however, it's clear they don't give a shit about the consumer, so I'm not holding my breath.
